shortDescription: Peru's central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 4.50% on Thursday, as expected, as officials warned that supply shocks, stronger inflation expectations and robust domestic demand were complicating the return of price growth to target.

children: Peru's central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 4.50% on Thursday, as expected, as officials warned that supply shocks, stronger inflation expectations and robust domestic demand were complicating the return of price growth to target.
Annual inflation rose to 5.3% in October from 4.5% in September, driven mainly by food and energy prices
12-month inflation expectations stood at 3.1%, slightly above the upper end of the bank's target range
Peru's central bank targets inflation between 1% and 3%
Thursday's rate hike, which was expected by the market, follows over a year of holding the rate at 4.25%, though the monetary authority had recently signaled concern over rising prices
Even so, the bank said Thursday's increase does not necessarily signal the start of a sustained tightening cycle
It said inflation and core inflation should return to the target range and move toward 2% as supply shocks fade
It warned that El Niño and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East could have persistent effects on prices
